messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: The record DOI/URL exactly matches the DOI reported in the HERO entry: 10.1016/j.seppur.2016.09.012 / https://doi.org/10.1016/j.seppur.2016.09.012.
The abstract explicitly states that PFOS and PFOA are recovered "from dilute water solution" using foam flotation, matching the matrix description of dilute aqueous PFOS and PFOA solutions.
The abstract clearly identifies the surfactants as Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and Perfluorooctanoate (PFOA), matching both PFAS listed in the record.

The abstract states that separation and recovery of PFOS and [SOURCE_TEXT_OMITTED sha256=826e45a1691e2763a2de0b485eaee48f95c282fdb52e28ea3386926552bf9fed])" and highlights ferric ion (Fe(III)) as activator, which matches the treatment description.

The abstract reports "removal efficiency" of PFOS and PFOA by foam flotation, describing physical removal from solution. Coding this as a removal endpoint is consistent with the described measurements and not contradicted by the source.

The abstract refers to "the separation and recovery" and gives a percentage of PFOS and PFOA recovered from the concentrate scum, which is appropriately coded as a separation/recovery endpoint and is consistent with the source language.

The abstract lists metallic activators as "Al(III), Fe(III), La(III), Ca(II), Fe(II), and K(I)", matching the value string. The qualifier describing the PFOS removal order Fe(III) ≈ La(III) > Al(III) > Ca(II) > Fe(II) > K(I) aligns with the reported order (Fe(III) La(III) > Al(III) > Ca(II) > Fe(II) > K(I)).
No numeric quantity is associated with the list of metallic activators, so leaving unit as null is appropriate and consistent with the abstract.
The abstract states that both PFOS and PFOA [SOURCE_TEXT_OMITTED sha256=5c540bc3ba7b521b4d845b6727f7d5d02d391eac6eafe2d958a789c7444bfc72]," matching the Fe(III) dose value of 11.5.
The Fe(III) dose is reported as 11.5 mM in the abstract; using "mM" as the unit is correct.
The abstract states that >99% removal occurred "in 5 min" at 11.5 mM Fe(III); thus, the contact time value of 5 is supported.
The time is reported in minutes ("in 5 min") in the abstract, so using "min" as the unit is correct.
The abstract notes that PFOS and PFOA removal increased with decreasing pH with maximum removal at "the lowest pH of 2.3 studied"; representing feed pH as 2.3 is directly supported.
pH is dimensionless; leaving the unit as an empty string is a benign representation and does not conflict with the source.

The abstract states that no significant removal was observed at pH ≥ 6, indicating a range. Recording a single value of 6 captures the threshold but not the full range (≥ 6), so the core idea is supported but the scope is simplified.
pH is dimensionless; use of an empty string as unit does not conflict with the source description.

This condition describes a qualitative trend (effect of Fe(III) dose) without specifying a numeric value; leaving the value field empty is consistent with the qualitative statement in the abstract that high Fe(III) dose enhanced surfactant removal.
No quantitative dose is given for this trend beyond the separately recorded 11.5 mM; leaving the unit null for a qualitative trend is appropriate.

The abstract qualitatively states that elevated initial PFOS and PFOA concentration enhanced surfactant removal, without providing a specific numeric concentration; leaving the numeric value empty is consistent with the qualitative nature of this condition.
Because no specific numeric initial concentration is reported in the cited text, omitting a unit for this qualitative trend is appropriate.
The abstract states: "[SOURCE_TEXT_OMITTED sha256=98fd20ce9aab0fc4e829fc270efadb32d2a4e69607c46f7fca3fe4dace1fe347]," directly supporting a pH value of 7.0 for the scum during recovery.
pH is dimensionless; an empty string for the unit is acceptable and not inconsistent with the source.
The abstract reports that both PFOS and PFOA had a removal efficiency of "> 99%" at 11.5 mM Fe(III) in 5 min. The value ">99" with inequality form matches this statement for PFOS.
Removal efficiency is expressed as a percentage in the abstract (>99%), so using "%" as the unit is correct.
The same abstract sentence states that both PFOS and PFOA had a removal efficiency of "> 99%" under the specified conditions; recording ">99" as an inequality for PFOA is directly supported.
As with PFOS, PFOA removal efficiency is expressed as a percentage; unit "%" is appropriate.

The abstract states that by adjusting scum pH to 7.0, "approximately 84–91% of PFOS and PFOA could be recovered." The recorded range value "84-91" matches this, with the approximation conveyed in qualifiers.
Recovery is reported as a percentage in the abstract (84–91%); using "%" as the unit is correct.

The study clearly reports bench-type foam flotation removal and recovery percentages for PFOS and PFOA in dilute aqueous solutions under specified Fe(III) dose and pH conditions. Inferring that these data are comparable with conditions to other bench-scale foam fractionation studies is a reasonable synthesis judgment supported by the reported matrix, treatment, and endpoints.

The stated comparability rationale accurately reflects the information in the abstract (dilute aqueous matrix, PFOS/PFOA, Fe(III) dose, contact time, and reported removal/recovery) and correctly notes missing reactor-geometry/gas-flow details, which is consistent with the limited abstract information.

The abstract and source limitations indicate that only PFOS and PFOA in dilute water solutions with metallic activators were studied, and the HERO page does not show data for other matrices or PFAS. Inferring this as a design-based limitation is consistent with the available information.

The EPA HERO page limitation notes that only abstract and bibliographic information were accessible and that detailed column geometry and gas flow were not available. The recorded limitation accurately reflects this lack of reactor and hydrodynamic details.

The abstract does not report the experimental scale, so noting that scale is "not reported" is supported. However, the added parenthetical interpretation that it "appears to be laboratory" introduces an inference not explicitly stated in the abstract, making the field only partially supported.
The HERO record classifies the publication as a primary experimental study (peer-reviewed article describing experiments), consistent with coding as "primary_experiment."

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements—source identity, PFAS analytes, aqueous matrix, foam flotation with metallic activators, operating conditions (pH, Fe(III) dose, contact time), and quantitative removal and recovery data—are all directly supported by the cited abstract text. Minor issues (e.g., simplification of the pH ≥ 6 range and inferred scale) do not affect the integrity of the quantitative findings or endpoint definitions, so the record is usable for synthesis with attention to noted qualifiers.
